cells.tense: The person is here at the work, deciding as it comes, and the hand is steady on it.
cells.ask: Say one intention out loud to someone close, in plain words, and let them hear what it's been costing.
cells.core:
The clearing has happened. The thing that couldn't hold is gone, the ground is level, and the person is on it — tending what grows now, deciding calmly among competing demands, not forcing any of them. That steadiness is easy to miss from the inside because it doesn't feel like work. Care is going out into something real, and it's coming back.

Steady work like this can feed one more thing: being seen. The person has been holding more than one demand at once and making it look ordinary, and one intention said out loud to someone close costs little and hands back their own measure of what they carried.

cells.verb: Tending what's growing with steady, responsible care

cells.tense: The person is braced against a future that hasn't happened, trying to hold it early.
cells.ask: Pick one demand and set it down for a day — leave the thing asking for attention untouched and let the day go on without it.
cells.core:
The clearing happened, and the person is holding the ground alone and bracing. More gets taken on than the season asks for, everything that could go wrong gets watched, calming the thing that hasn't happened becomes the work — and the care stops being about anything that grows. It's about staying ahead of it. The parent here holds space without gripping, and the grip is this.

Waiting on the other side is ease that came from somewhere real — satisfaction from what was lived, not managed. The move is small: pick one demand and set it down for a day, leave it untouched, and let the day go on. A little room opens to be in your own life instead of a step ahead of it.

cells.tense: The person is standing at a door that is already behind them, still taking instructions from the far side of it.
cells.ask: Each morning this week, tend one growing thing and no other — one small, concrete, specific thing, chosen new each day.
cells.core:
Something cleared and the person stepped back from it instead of forward. Watering went quiet. Two demands got dropped rather than carried together, and the daily deciding of what to water stopped, because carrying it happened somewhere ahead of where the person came to rest.

What's starved here is hope for the direction, not effort. Persistence doesn't get called up; it comes back when the person is still aimed at something. So start with one morning at a time: tend one growing thing today and no other, then one tomorrow. The ground under it returns — the sense of being aimed at something again.

cells.tense: The person is already deciding what gets tended and saying it's happening on its own.
cells.ask: Write one sentence beginning 'I chose ___', naming one thing done here lately, and put it where someone else will see it.
cells.core:
Something cleared, and the person moved — kept some things, lay others down, chose where to stand — and the decision is working. It's just being described as circumstance. What happened was done by someone, and that someone got left out of the account. Calling it luck or a season is the misattribution this line runs into.

So put the doer back on something smaller than the whole life and concrete: one sentence beginning 'I chose ___', naming one thing done lately, somewhere a witness will see it. Being acknowledged works on the person as much as for anyone — and what's been happening finally gets named by the one who did it.

attempts.check: The riskiest claim is that the person is carrying two demands at once — the card's number says two demands held in balance, but the record does not say this person has any particular pair, so I keep it as what the capacity looks like, not as a fact about their life. A reader could reasonably say the collapse they have been standing next to was a loss and not a liberation; the cells never call it one, and every ask — one demand released, one plain intent said out loud, one outcome written on paper, one thing named in front of a witness — is useful even if my read of the condition is wrong. The sentence that serves the writer more than the reader is the story about how long they have been braced; I cut it, and the tense lines carry the position in time only. The ask under Too Much must not push effort or feeling into the emptied seat; it hands the seat's work back, which is the vertical mechanism run the other way.
